lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが半濁点、つまり「゜」の使い方を教えて下さるわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad is going to show you how to use the handakuten — that little circle mark.
lines.style: Warm, matter-of-fact clarity. Slight lift on Sho's name to draw his attention. Calm pace, like sharing something pleasant she knows he'll enjoy.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんと片仮名のヽ、つまり繰り返し記号で遊んだよ
lines.en: Mom, I played with Dad using the katakana iteration mark — the repeating symbol!
lines.style: Bright, eager clip to the opening. Small-kid energy — bouncing slightly on the words. Genuine excitement about the game, not performing it. Quick pace.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが平仮名のゞ、つまり濁点繰り返しを書いて下さるわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad is going to write the hiragana voiced iteration mark for you.
lines.style: Soft, thoughtful tone. Slight pause before the key phrase, as if watching Sho process. Warm but unhurried. The rhythm of a mother who knows her child is taking it in.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんに平仮名のゝ、つまり繰り返し記号を教えて頂いたよ
lines.en: Mom, Dad taught me the hiragana iteration mark — the repeating symbol!
lines.style: Earnest, deliberate. Pride in having learned something, not boasting. Clear enunciation on the key terms, like wanting to say them right. Steady, genuine energy.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんがヾ、つまり片仮名の濁点繰り返しを見せて下さったわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad showed you the katakana voiced iteration mark.
lines.style: Reflective, observing. Slight wonder in the tone — acknowledging what her husband has shared. Unhurried pace. The voice of a mother noting a small, meaningful moment.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんに旧仮名のゐ、つまり「い」の古形を教えて頂いたよ
lines.en: Mom, Dad taught me the old kana wi — the ancient form of い.
lines.style: Earnest, careful delivery of the term. Concentrated on getting it right. Not rushed, but focused. The sincere effort of a young child learning something special.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが古文のゐる、つまり「いる」を読んで下さったわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad read the classical wi-ru form to you — the old way of saying いる.
lines.style: Calm, slightly wondering tone. Letting the moment breathe. Warm appreciation for what Ryosuke is teaching. Gentle, unhurried pace.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんに爾、つまり古文の「それ」の意味を教えて頂いたよ
lines.en: Mom, Dad taught me the meaning of 爾 — that old word for 'that' in classical Japanese!
lines.style: Eager, pleased conclusion. Bright on the final phrase. Small laugh in the delivery — delighted to have learned something old and specific. Quick, genuine energy.
